questions.question: A man walks 10 m East, then 10 m North and then 10 m West. He is now ___ from the starting point.
questions.explanation: The East and West legs cancel. He is 10 m North of the start.

questions.question: Facing North, a person turns right. He now faces
questions.explanation: A right turn is clockwise: North → East.

questions.question: Facing East, a person turns left. He now faces
questions.explanation: A left turn is anticlockwise: East → North.

questions.question: In the morning, a man stands facing the rising sun. His shadow falls towards the
questions.explanation: The sun is in the East, and a shadow falls opposite the sun: towards the West (behind him).

questions.question: The direction opposite to North-west is
questions.explanation: The opposite of North is South and of West is East, so the opposite of North-west is South-east.

questions.question: A man walks 3 km North, turns right and walks 4 km. His distance from the start is
questions.explanation: The legs are at right angles: √(3² + 4²) = 5 km.

questions.question: A man walks 6 km East and then 8 km North. His straight-line distance from the start is
A man walks 15 m West, turns right and walks 20 m, then turns right again and walks 15 m. He is now ___ from the starting point.
questions.explanation: West 15 m: (−15, 0). Right turn from West faces North: 20 m gives (−15, 20). Right turn from North faces East: 15 m gives (0, 20). He is 20 m North of the start.

questions.question: A person facing North turns 90° clockwise and then 180° anticlockwise. He now faces
questions.explanation: North turned 90° clockwise faces East. Turned 180° anticlockwise from East he faces West.

questions.question: A man faces West. He turns left, then right, then right again. He now faces
questions.explanation: West → left → South → right → West → right → North.

questions.question: Two friends start from the same point. A walks 12 km North and B walks 16 km East. The distance between them is
Ravi walks 4 km South, then 3 km West, then 4 km North. How far is he from the start?
questions.explanation: The South and North legs cancel. He is 3 km West of the start.

questions.question: A man goes 10 m South, turns left and goes 20 m, then turns left and goes 10 m. He is now ___ from the start.
questions.explanation: South 10 m: (0, −10). Left from South faces East: (20, −10). Left from East faces North: (20, 0). He is 20 m East of the start.

questions.question: At sunset, the shadow of a pole falls towards the
questions.explanation: At sunset the sun is in the West, and the shadow falls opposite, towards the East.

questions.question: Raj walks 8 km North, then 6 km East, then 8 km South and then 3 km West. He is now ___ from his house.
questions.explanation: North and South legs cancel (8 − 8 = 0). East − West = 6 − 3 = 3 km East.

questions.question: A walks 20 m East, turns right and walks 10 m, turns right and walks 20 m, then turns left and walks 5 m. His distance from the start is
questions.explanation: East 20: (20, 0). Right → South 10: (20, −10). Right → West 20: (0, −10). Left from West faces South: 5 m gives (0, −15). He is 15 m South of the start.

questions.question: A man walks 3 km North, 4 km East, 6 km South and then 4 km West. He is now ___ from the start.
questions.explanation: North − South = 3 − 6 = 3 km South. East − West = 4 − 4 = 0.

questions.question: A man walks 13 km East, then 12 km North, then 8 km West. His distance from the start is
questions.explanation: Net East = 13 − 8 = 5 km, net North = 12 km. Distance = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 km.

questions.question: Suresh is facing South-west. He turns 90° clockwise. He now faces
questions.explanation: Clockwise turns go South-west → West → North-west. So a 90° clockwise turn from South-west faces North-west.

questions.question: A is 5 km North of B. C is 5 km East of B. In which direction is C from A?
questions.explanation: Taking B as the origin, A = (0, 5) and C = (5, 0). From A to C is 5 km East and 5 km South, i.e. South-east.
